quotes.text: Worst damnfool mistake I ever made was letting myself be elected Vice President of the United States. Should have stuck with my old chores as Speaker of the House. I gave up the second most important job in the Government for one that didn't amount to a hill of beans. I spent eight long years as Mr. Roosevelt's spare tire.
quotes.speaker: John Nance Garner
quotes.context: FDR's first vice president ("Cactus Jack"), ruefully mocking his own decision to take the job and his powerlessness in it, after leaving office.

quotes.text: When I was governor, someone put a bill on my desk that was eighty-three pages long. Page eighty-two was where they hid the thing they actually wanted.

quotes.context: Panel discussion at the Aspen Ideas Festival, Aspen, Colorado, June 2019, recorded by The Atlantic

The giveaway is the specificity of 'page eighty-two,' which is just slightly too precise to be a natural off-the-cuff number.

quotes.text: Constituent mail is a fascinating document. People write to me about the price of eggs. They write to me about the geese on the National Mall. Both feel equally urgent to them, and honestly, I'm not sure they're wrong.
quotes.speaker: Bernie Sanders
quotes.context: Conversation with Ezra Klein on The Ezra Klein Show, New York Times Audio, September 2022

quotes.text: An old friend of mine once told me, you know, just be yourself - unless you suck.
quotes.speaker: John Kennedy
quotes.context: Republican U.S. Senator from Louisiana, known for his folksy one-liners, sharing a piece of self-deprecating advice. He used the line in a Jan. 25, 2018 Fox News interview. Innocuous and funny, with no target or policy edge.

source.title: 15 times Sen. John Kennedy got folksy, snarky or both | nola.com

quotes.text: Few thought he was even a starter / There were many who thought themselves smarter / But he ended PM / CH and OM / An earl and a knight of the garter.
quotes.speaker: Clement Attlee
quotes.context: A self-mocking limerick the former British PM wrote about himself in a letter to his brother Tom Attlee, April 8, 1956.
